rules.title: State minimum wage rises to $17.40/hour on January 1, 2027
rules.plain_english: From January 1, 2027, every California employer must pay at least $17.40 an hour for all hours worked, up from $16.90 in 2026. If the city or county where the work is done has a higher minimum wage, pay the higher rate.
rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their employees, including construction contractors
rules.citation: Labor Code 1182.12 (annual inflation adjustment); DIR News Release No. 2026-66 (Aug. 13, 2026)
rules.source_location: https://www.dir.ca.gov/DIRNews/2026/2026-66.html (News Release No. 2026-66, dated August 13, 2026, first paragraph); prior 2026 rate: https://www.dir.ca.gov/iwc/MW-2026.pdf (MW-2026: 'Effective January 1, 2026, Minimum Wage: $16.90 per hour')
rules.verbatim_quote: Beginning January 1, 2027, California’s statewide minimum wage will increase to $17.40 per hour, helping wages keep pace with inflation and providing greater economic support to workers across the state.
rules.notes: The release says DOF certified the increase on July 31, 2026. The DOF certification letter is on dof.ca.gov, which this session cannot reach. The MW-2027 poster (https://www.dir.ca.gov/iwc/MW-2027.pdf) returned 404 on 2026-11-25, so the 2027 posting text and the 2027 meal and lodging credits are not yet published. The increase, day, week and 2x figures are arithmetic, not quotes. The 2x figure is the 2027 test in the existing rule tools-equipment-employer-provides.

No value changed: $17.40 from 2027-01-01, DOF certification on July 31, 2026 and piece-rate coverage are in the release. The 0.50, 139.20, 696.00 and 34.80 figures were recomputed from 17.40.

rules.title: Exempt (white-collar) employees must earn at least $72,384 a year from January 1, 2027
rules.plain_english: To treat an office manager, estimator or other salaried employee as exempt from overtime in 2027, you must pay at least $72,384 a year ($1,392 a week), and the job must also pass the duties test.

parameters.also_required: duties and other requirements of the specific exemption

rules.applies_to: Employers classifying employees as exempt executive, administrative or professional employees
rules.citation: DIR News Release No. 2026-66 (Aug. 13, 2026); Labor Code 515; IWC Order 16-2001 §1(A) (as cited in the existing rule exempt-salary-threshold-2026)
rules.source_location: https://www.dir.ca.gov/DIRNews/2026/2026-66.html (section 'Minimum salary requirement for exempt employees'); prior 2026 figure: computed from https://www.dir.ca.gov/iwc/MW-2026.pdf ($16.90) and https://www.dir.ca.gov/IWC/IWCArticle16.pdf §1(A) (two times the state minimum wage for full-time employment)
rules.verbatim_quote: Beginning January 1, 2027, an employee must earn an annual salary of at least $72,384 to meet the salary threshold for exemption. Employees must also satisfy the duties and other requirements applicable to the specific exemption.
rules.notes: The release shows the formula: $17.40 x 2 x 40 hours per week x 52 weeks per year = $72,384. The monthly and weekly figures are arithmetic. This rule updates exempt-salary-threshold-2026 for 2027. The prior 2026 figure ($70,304) is not printed in the release; it is 2 x $16.90 (MW-2026) x 40 x 52 under IWC Order 16 §1(A).

rules.title: Reimburse all necessary work expenses and losses (Labor Code 2802)
rules.plain_english: If a worker spends their own money or loses property because they did the job or followed your instructions, you must pay them back. Examples include required insurance, bank fees for required direct deposit, required uniforms and business use of a personal vehicle.

parameters.reimburse: all necessary expenditures or losses incurred in direct consequence of the discharge of duties or obedience to the employer's directions
parameters.test: expense or loss incurred within the course and scope of employment (respondeat superior)
examples_per_dlse: cost of opening or operating a bank account required for direct deposit (O.L. 1997.03.21-2)
business use of the employee's car (mileage)
legal costs of defending a third-party action based on job-related conduct
employee-owned tools stolen from the employer's premises when trade custom required the employee to supply them and they were too heavy to carry home

rules.applies_to: All California employers

rules.plain_english: When workers drive their own vehicles for work, paying the IRS mileage rate normally satisfies the law. If a worker proves their real costs were higher, for example because you require extra insurance, you must pay the difference. Paying less than the IRS rate is presumed not to comply unless you prove actual costs were lower.

rules.plain_english: You may take money out of a paycheck only when the law requires it (taxes, garnishments), when the worker agreed in writing to pay for things like insurance or benefit plans, or when a union or wage agreement authorizes health, welfare or pension contributions.
